purpose: Test whether C1/N1 synthetic probability quality depends on the correct rider-to-line-structure mapping rather than generic model flexibility.
scope: source-independent Digital Twin W0-W4 synthetic failure diagnostic only
expected_invariants: C0 predictions are exactly unchanged by structure scrambling
all probability objects keep complete support and unit mass
C1 and N1 keep the same rank-1 marginal within each PRE condition
every rider receives a different complete structure slot while the slot multiset is preserved

diagnostic_interpretation_only: C0 remained exactly invariant, confirming the transform changed only structure fields ignored by C0.
N1 intact structure scored better than scrambled structure in 19 of 20 world-by-seed-block cells.
N1 mean scramble penalty was much larger in relational W2-W4 than in W0, consistent with N1 using the intended line-relation mechanism inside the engineered synthetic worlds.
C1 also showed smaller structure sensitivity, consistent with its line-position utility term.
This is a synthetic mechanism-sensitivity negative control, not real-keirin causal evidence, model-selection evidence, or promotion authority.

reported_diagnostic: scrambled minus intact expected ordered-top3 log loss by world and seed block; positive means intact structure scored better
pass_criterion: execution and invariants only; PASS does not require any sign or ranking outcome
